cases.title: Everything on your boarding pass

skeleton.brief: Boarding passes look like receipts but hide secret info
Explain boarding pass fields serve hidden purposes
Passenger name matches reservation exactly, middle initial matters
Flight number encodes airline and direction with even/odd digits
Seat letter shows boarding group, affecting bag handling
Corner string signals security screening level before airport
Barcode stores personal data unencrypted, risky to share
Each field added due to past problems
Understanding boarding pass reveals hidden travel insights

narration.text: A boarding pass looks like a receipt, but almost every field on it is doing something you were never told about.

slot_quote.heading: A boarding pass looks like a receipt, but almost every field on it is doing something you were never told about.

narration.text: Each field on a boarding pass serves a hidden purpose beyond what you see. They encode information about your flight, status, and security that helps airlines and airports operate smoothly.

asset_request.description: a clean, centered boarding pass on plain background with no text
asset_request.guidance: A clear, well-lit photo of a single boarding pass on a plain background, no text overlays.

narration.text: The passenger name matches the reservation exactly. That middle initial can actually matter at the gate, not just the first and last names.

slot_myth_fact.myth: The middle initial on a boarding pass doesn't matter.
slot_myth_fact.fact: The passenger name must match the reservation exactly, including middle initial.
slot_myth_fact.heading: Passenger Name Accuracy

narration.text: The flight number encodes the airline's two-letter code plus up to four digits. Even numbers usually indicate eastbound or northbound flights, odd numbers the return leg.
The seat letter shows your boarding group, which is set by fare class and status. This is the only field that determines how your bag is handled.

slot_stat.heading: Seat Letter Indicates Boarding Group
bullets: Boarding group affects bag handling and boarding order.

narration.text: A short string in the corner, like S or SSSS, signals your security screening level before you even reach the airport.

asset_request.description: boarding pass corner showing security screening string
asset_request.guidance: Close-up photo of a boarding pass corner highlighting the security screening string, clear and focused.

narration.text: The barcode at the bottom is not encrypted. It stores your name, record locator, and frequent flyer number in plain text, so sharing photos of your pass is risky.

asset_request.description: boarding pass barcode close-up
asset_request.guidance: Close-up image of a boarding pass barcode, clear and sharp, showing the barcode area.

narration.text: Every one of these fields was added because something went wrong once. They are solutions to past problems in air travel.

slot_receipt.heading: Fields Added Due to Past Problems
slot_receipt.caption: Each field addresses a specific issue encountered in air travel.

narration.text: Understanding your boarding pass reveals hidden travel insights that help you navigate the airport and protect your personal data.

asset_request.description: traveler holding boarding pass at airport gate
asset_request.guidance: A natural photo of a traveler holding a boarding pass at an airport gate, showing the pass clearly but not close-up.

cases.title: Four cities, four front doors

skeleton.brief: Every city has a personality shown in its front doors
Introduce front doors as reflections of city character
Amsterdam doors lean forward with hoisting beams for furniture
Marrakesh doors are heavy, blank, facing inward to courtyards
Kyoto doors use wooden lattice and sliding paper screens
Reykjavik houses painted bright to combat scarce winter light
Each door solves a unique local problem, not just decoration
Vernacular architecture evolves through many small, lived corrections

narration.text: Every city has a personality, and you can read it off the front doors.

asset_request.description: a variety of colorful front doors from different cities
asset_request.guidance: A vibrant, well-lit photo showing diverse front doors from multiple cities, avoiding overly staged or artificial looks.

narration.text: Front doors reflect the character of their cities. They tell stories about the people and the environment around them.
In Amsterdam, houses lean forward over the canals. They are narrow and tall, with a hoisting beam at the top because the staircases were too tight to carry furniture up.

asset_request.description: narrow tall Amsterdam houses leaning over a canal with hoisting beams
asset_request.guidance: A clear photo of Amsterdam canal houses showing the leaning facade and hoisting beam, preferably in daylight.

narration.text: In Marrakesh, the street front is almost blank. Heavy studded doors face inward to courtyards, keeping family life private and protected from the outside world.

asset_request.description: heavy studded Marrakesh door
asset_request.guidance: A detailed photo of a heavy, studded door typical in Marrakesh, showing texture and craftsmanship.

asset_request.description: Marrakesh courtyard hidden behind doors
asset_request.guidance: A photo showing a private courtyard behind a door in Marrakesh, emphasizing privacy.

asset_request.description: Marrakesh street with blank facades
asset_request.guidance: A street view in Marrakesh showing blank facades and minimal street-facing windows.

narration.text: Kyoto doors use wooden lattice screens and sliding paper doors, creating a boundary that can be opened by just a hand’s width.
In Reykjavik, houses are wrapped in corrugated iron and painted bright colors to brighten the scarce winter light.

asset_request.description: Reykjavik houses painted in bright colors with corrugated iron
asset_request.guidance: A vivid photo of brightly painted Reykjavik houses with corrugated iron siding, in winter light.

narration.text: Each door solves a unique local problem, not just decoration.

slot_stat.heading: Not Just Decoration
bullets: Each door addresses a local challenge

narration.text: Vernacular architecture evolves through thousands of small, lived corrections, each improving on the last.

slot_counter.heading: Thousands of Corrections
bullets: Small changes made by everyday people
